Maintenance Report — MNT-0184-005

Asset: WELL-0184 (NE-08 Well 184, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 22 Sep 2023 08:00 · Finished: 22 Sep 2023 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 11 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0184-0049 on 2023-09-21 Report written: 24 Sep 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0184-0049 at 10:15 on 2023-09-21 found crude oil on the pad: about 4.9% of the pad area, estimated 2.4 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 391 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 313 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.7 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0184-005 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.54% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0184-017

Asset: WELL-0184 (NE-08 Well 184, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 05 Oct 2025 08:00 · Finished: 15 Oct 2025 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 251 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0184-0153 on 2025-10-02 Report written: 17 Oct 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw a thin film of oil on the wellhead. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0184-0153 showed the wellhead at 28.1 °C with the air at 24.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Normal packing wear.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0184-020

Asset: WELL-0184 (NE-08 Well 184, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 24 Jan 2026 08:00 · Finished: 10 Feb 2026 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 419 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0184-0167 on 2026-01-22 Report written: 11 Feb 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0184-0167 showed the wellhead at 10.2 °C with the air at 5.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 15 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.
